source.title: Irish News, 6 June 1939, p. 5 ("Council's vice-chairman: Nationalists ask for 'fair play'", annual meeting of Lisnaskea Rural District Council)
source.check: Read on the page image (INA block image): at the annual meeting on Monday 5 June 1939, the first after the election, 'Mr. Owen Hanna (N.)' takes part as a member; the three members co-opted that day are named (Joseph Johnston, John Johnston, John Hurst, all Unionists), so Hanna sat as an elected member.

note: Triennial rural district council election, end of May 1939; there was no contest in the Lisnaskea district (Northern Whig, 4 May 1939, p. 10). Armagh Manor is the one division missing from the Northern Whig's list of the thirty members returned (4 May 1939, p. 10: eighteen Unionists and twelve Nationalists), and there was no contest in the district. Owen Hanna, returned for Armagh Manor in 1936, is not named for any other division, so he is placed in Armagh Manor by elimination (inferred). If no nomination was made there, he was deemed re-elected as the retiring member.
